_meta.name: MASQUE extraction development set
_meta.provenance: AUTHORED — written by hand to probe known failure modes. NOT openFDA, NOT FAERS, NOT patient data. Numbers computed on this set are development figures for guiding rule changes; they are NOT validation results and must not be reported as extraction performance on real narratives. Cases added in 0.3.0 were drafted by the screenAIr team to exercise the phrases and behaviours the clinical lead approved on 2026-10-04; the case text itself has not yet been reviewed by the clinical lead. The cases added in round 2 of 0.3.0 (design 05 §12) were drafted by the team in the same way and have not been reviewed by the clinical lead either. The cases added in round 3 of 0.3.0 (rules R9-R11, design 05 §13) were drafted by the team in the same way and have not been reviewed by the clinical lead either. The same holds for the cases added in rounds 3b and 3c (design 05 §13.10, §13.11).
_meta.labelling: Single author, no adjudication. A real benchmark needs >=2 independent annotators with an inter-annotator agreement statistic; that is a stated gap, not an oversight.

registers.encounter: patient speech in clinic, first person
registers.narrative: third-person clinical prose, approximating a FAERS narrative

revisionLog: 0.2.0 — three labels corrected after the first benchmark run disagreed with them and the extractor turned out to be right. Recorded rather than silently amended: a gold set edited to match its system is not a gold set, so every change is listed with its reason.
0.3.0 — 156 utterances and 53 dialogues added for lexicon 0.3.2 (F1 heard, F2 carry-over, F3 vocabulary, F4 yield, text normalization); no 0.2.0 case or label changed.

0.3.0 round 2 (2026-10-04, design 05 §12) — 40 utterances (t001-t040) and 19 dialogues (d054-d072) added for the round-2 rules (R1 carry negation clause-wide, R2 band choice for heard entries, R3a carryExclude, R3b onset guard, R4 digits for durations only, R5 yield after the heard card is answered or skipped), the red-flag and mixed normalize cases, and every trace of the round-1 review, including the disclosed known risks. Six labels changed with the round-2 rules; as for every 0.3.0 label, each is the extractor's output under those rules: u008 and u009 (R4: digits no longer reach the i_days cue "ten days" or the v_count phrase "five episodes"), d010 (R1), d021, d039 and d041 (R3a). Each changed case says so in its note. No 0.2.0 case or label changed. Totals: 196 utterances and 72 dialogues added to the 44 cases of 0.2.0. (The wording of this entry was corrected in round 3, review F8.)

0.3.0 round 3 (2026-10-05, design 05 §13) — 16 utterances (w001-w016) and 13 dialogues (d073-d085) added for the round-3 rules (R9 direct extraction for heard entries: a negated band span, a carryRefuse phrase or disagreeing spans withhold the value, and an utterance whose value was withheld while a band span was present opens no carry-over and closes an open slot of that item; R10 carry: carryExclude phrases count for the negation and disagreement tests, and any negated span refuses the whole reply; R11 a carryExclude phrase counts in direct extraction only in the sentence of the cue), every trace of the round-2 review (F1-F4, ENG-R1-1), the R11 boundary rule and its disclosed exception, and the compound-tens known risk. Four labels changed with the round-3 rules; as for every 0.3.0 label, each is the extractor's output under those rules: t003 and t005 (R9: a negated band span withholds the value) and d069 and d070 (R9: no carry-over opens from an utterance whose value was withheld while a band span was present). Each changed case says so in its note. The notes of t001, t009, t011, t012, t013, y014, d010, d021, d039, d041, d050, d059 and d065 were corrected for the round-3 rules; their labels are unchanged. No 0.2.0 case or label changed. Totals: 212 utterances and 85 dialogues added to the 44 cases of 0.2.0.

0.3.0 round 3b (2026-10-05, design 05 §13.10) — 5 dialogues (d086-d090) added for the yield-only slot: an utterance whose duration is withheld (a negated band span, a carryRefuse phrase or disagreeing spans) arms a slot that keeps the entries yielding to the item yielding but is never carried into, and turns an open slot of the item yield-only with its remaining count instead of closing it; the dialogue format gains the pending form [id, turnsLeft, "yield-only"]. Seven dialogue labels changed with the round-3b rule; as for every 0.3.0 label, each is the extractor's output under those rules: d069, d070, d075, d076, d078 and d079 (the withheld line now arms a yield-only slot; round 3 armed none) and d085 (the open slot turns yield-only instead of closing). Only their pending labels and notes changed; no capture, heard or refusal label changed. Each changed dialogue says so in its note. No utterance case and no 0.2.0 case or label changed. The added dialogues were drafted by the team in the same way as the other 0.3.0 cases and have not been reviewed by the clinical lead. Totals: 212 utterances and 90 dialogues added to the 44 cases of 0.2.0.

0.3.0 round 3c (2026-10-05, design 05 §13.11) — 6 utterances (w017-w022) and 3 dialogues (d091-d093) added for two corrections found by the final pre-deploy review. (1) R11 made removal-only: a carryExclude phrase supplies a value in direct extraction only in a cue sentence (one holding a hit of any of the entry's cue phrases that is not negated and passes the attribution and history gates), and elsewhere it still counts for the negation and disagreement tests and as a stated band, so the entry is withheld and opens only a yield-only slot. Round 3 ignored such a span entirely, which let an overlapping "days at a time" score Over 72 h and let carry-over open after a day range (reviews F-R11-OVER72, ENG-R11-1), and took the cue's sentence from the first-listed cue phrase found only (ENG-R11-2). (2) A yield-only slot of a withheld entry is refreshed with the full carry on each withheld line, instead of keeping its remaining count (review F-3B-REMAINING-COUNT). Labels changed with these rules; as for every 0.3.0 label, each is the extractor's output under them: w013 (now heard, no value; round 3 recorded v 1), d077 (the first line opens only a yield-only slot and the reply is not carried; round 3 carried v 2), d085 and d088 (the converted slot is refreshed), d089 (m_dur now yields on the last line; round 3b recorded m_dur = Under 4 h). The notes of w003, w005, w006, w007, w008 and w009 were corrected; their labels are unchanged. No 0.2.0 case or label changed. The added cases were drafted by the team and have not been reviewed by the clinical lead. Totals: 218 utterances and 93 dialogues added to the 44 cases of 0.2.0.
_meta.labels030: Each 0.3.0 label is what lexicon 0.3.2 with the screenAIr 0.4.1 extractor (round 2, round 3, round 3b and round 3c rules included) returns: the 0.3.0 labels are the 0.3.2 extractor's own output (regression snapshot); P/R/F1 on them is tautological, not a measurement. Known false positives, false suppressions and misses are labelled as the rule behaves and carry a note, as z02 and z04 do in 0.2.0. Labels are development data, not ground truth for performance claims.

format.cases: Run with extract(lexicon, text, {includeHeard: true}), unsuppressed. expect: the item, ctx and red-flag [id, value] pairs (a set). expectHeard: the heard ids (a set; [] when absent).
format.dialogues: turns: [speaker, text], speaker pt (patient) or md (physician). Patient turns run through extractInContext(lexicon, text, pending) in order, keeping the returned pending; md turns are passed over and leave pending untouched, as in the Scribe. Also as in the Scribe (round 2, R5): a heard capture of an item already answered is dropped, and while the pending item is answered the slot is still passed, with {carry: false}, and the returned pending is kept. steps[k] labels turn k: null for an md turn, else {captures: [id, value] or [id, value, "carry"], in engine order; heard: heard ids; pending: [id, turnsLeft] after the turn, or [id, turnsLeft, "yield-only"] for a yield-only slot (round 3b: it counts as pending for yieldTo and is consumed and expires like any slot, but no value is ever carried into it), or null; refused: the carry refusal code or null}. As in the Scribe, the returned pending is kept and passed whole, yieldOnly included.

cases.text: The spinning lasts 3-4 minutes.
cases.note: Ranges stay digits, so only "minutes" (v 2) matches. Known limitation, labelled as the rule behaves.

cases.text: It hit me in a split second and the spinning lasted for hours
cases.note: R2, kept by R9 d: the band spans disagree ("split second" v 1, "hours" v 2), so no value is taken and the item stays heard. Since round 3 (R9 f) a band span was present, so no carry-over opens from it (d069; in round 2 it armed). Round 1 took v 1 by band order; 0.3.1 read v 2 (review F4).

cases.text: I get dizzy a couple minutes after standing up and it lasts for hours
cases.note: R2: "a couple minutes" (v 1; the contained "minutes" is dropped) and "hours" (v 2) disagree: heard, no value. Round 1: v 1 (review F4). m_dur's "lasts" yields to the v_vertigo cue.

cases.text: The dizziness is never under five minutes, it lasts hours
cases.note: Relabelled in round 3 (R9 b): "under five minutes" is negated within the window ("never"), and any negated band span withholds the value, so the item stays heard; a band span was present, so no carry-over opens (d079) and the clinician asks. Round 2 dropped the negated span and read v 2 from "hours"; round 1 read v 1, bands were not negation-checked (review F4).

cases.text: The dizziness lasts hours, sometimes all day.
cases.note: R2: two live spans ("hours", "all day") agree on v 2.

cases.text: I'm dizzy for a few seconds, not hours.
cases.note: Relabelled in round 3 (R9 b): "hours" is negated within the window, so no value is taken and no carry-over opens; the clinician asks. A disclosed recall cost: rounds 1 and 2 read v 1 ("few seconds"), round 2 after dropping the negated span.

cases.text: I'm dizzy for three days at a time.
cases.note: R2: "for three days" (v 2) and "days at a time" (v 3) overlap without either containing the other, so they disagree: heard, no value. Round 1: v 3 by band order.

cases.text: My headache lasts all day, maybe a week.
cases.note: R2 applies only to entries with heard: true. m_dur has no heard flag and keeps the first band in array order: "all day" (v 2) before "a week" (v 3).

cases.text: I felt dizzy a couple minutes ago
cases.note: R3b onset guard: the carryRefuse phrase "ago" withholds every band value of the utterance, so the item stays heard. Round 1: v 1, an onset read as a duration (review F4).

cases.text: The dizziness started about a day ago
cases.note: R3b onset guard ("started", "ago"; R9 c since round 3): heard, no value. Round 1: v 2 through "about a day" (review F7). Since round 3 (R9 f) a band span was present, so no carry-over opens and the reply after it is not carried (d070; in round 2 it was).

cases.text: I woke up with vertigo, it came on overnight
cases.note: Disclosed residual of the day-range risk: no carryRefuse phrase occurs, so the approved band "overnight" reads v 2 in the cue's own sentence (review F7; no new phrase was added).

cases.text: I've been dizzy for two days
cases.note: Disclosed residual of the day-range risk: an illness duration in the cue's own sentence. A carryExclude phrase still counts in direct extraction when it lies in the cue's own sentence (R11), so "for two days" still reads v 2 here (review F7).

cases.text: I've been dizzy since Monday, and it lasts hours.
cases.note: R3b recall cost (R9 c since round 3): "since" withholds the episode duration too; the item stays heard and unanswered, so it is still asked. Since round 3 (R9 f) a band span was present, so no carry-over opens from it and a later reply cannot supply a value (d076; review F3: in round 2 it armed, and "All week." was carried). m_dur's "lasts" yields.

cases.text: I got dizzy in Chicago for hours.
cases.note: R3b recall cost (R9 c since round 3): carryRefuse phrases match as substrings, so "ago" inside "Chicago" withholds the duration.
